title: Two-dimensional V2C@Se (MXene) composite cathode material for high-performance r

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly identifies the vanadium carbide MXene as V2C multiple times (e.g., title: “Two-dimensional V2C@Se (MXene)…”; abstract: “synthesized vanadium carbide (V2C)…”; Fig. 1 caption lists “V2C” and “V2C@Se”). Therefore the target formula V2C is directly supported, even though the alleged provenance page/figure description is slightly off (Fig. 1 caption appears on page 140 in the provided text).

The paper clearly identifies the studied/synthesized material as the two-dimensional V2C@Se (MXene) composite (title, abstract, Fig. 1 caption, and throughout). However, the Extracted Value for “Target Formula” is blank/empty, which is not supported as an extracted formula because the document does specify the target material formula.

The document explicitly identifies V2AlC as the MAX-phase precursor: “multilayer V2C was prepared by etching V2AlC…” and “selective etching aluminum element of V2AlC…” (Results/Discussion and Conclusion). Nowhere in the provided text is an explicit amount/mass/molar ratio given for V2AlC (or for the starting reagents), so “Amount: Not specified in text” is consistent with the source (per null-handling rule). The alleged provenance (Page 139 Fig.1 description) is not necessary/accurate for support; the support appears in the main text around the Fig. 1 discussion (pages 2–3 of the excerpt).

The paper explicitly states that V2C was synthesized by etching V2AlC using lithium fluoride and concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl) solution (e.g., Abstract: “etching with lithium fluoride and concentrated hydrochloric acid solution”; main text: “etching V2AlC with concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl) and lithium fluoride (LiF)”). However, nowhere in the provided full text is a specific amount/volume/molarity of concentrated HCl given. Therefore, identifying the chemical (hydrochloric acid, concentrated) with amount “Not specified in text” is supported. The alleged provenance pages are slightly off (the statement is on page 138 Abstract / page 139 text rather than a Fig.1 description), but the content is present in the document.

The paper clearly mentions lithium fluoride (LiF) as a reagent used to etch V2AlC (e.g., Abstract: “etching with lithium fluoride and concentrated hydrochloric acid solution”; and later: “etched … with … lithium fluoride (LiF)”). However, nowhere in the provided full text is an amount (mass, molarity, volume, etc.) of LiF specified. Therefore the extraction ‘Lithium fluoride | Amount: Not specified in text’ is supported. (Provenance is partially off: the LiF mention is in the Abstract on page 138 of the journal pagination, but not in the Fig. 1 caption/description.)

The paper clearly identifies selenium (Se) as part of the V2C@Se composite (e.g., abstract: “calcining with selenium”; Fig. 1 caption and multiple sections discuss Se). However, across the provided full text there is no explicit quantitative amount of selenium used (no mass, molar ratio, wt%, at%, loading, etc.) in the synthesis description. Therefore the extractor’s statement “Selenium | Amount: Not specified in text” is consistent with the document text.

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly describes an etching step in the synthesis: V2C is synthesized “through etching with lithium fluoride and concentrated hydrochloric acid solution” (Abstract) and “multilayer V2C was prepared by etching V2AlC with concentrated HCl and LiF” (Page 2). Therefore, the synthesis operation includes etching.

entity_reviews.extracted_value: description=Calcination of V2C with selenium to form V2C@Se composite.

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly describes a calcination step in the synthesis of the V2C@Se composite (e.g., “The composite two-dimensional layered structure (V2C@Se) is formed after calcining with selenium” and “V2C powder was calcined with selenium…”). Therefore the synthesis operation “calcine” is supported by the source text.

The paper explicitly states: “The BET result of V2C@Se is reduced from 7.6 m2 g−1 (V2C) to 5.3 m2 g−1, which is shown in Fig. S1.” This directly supports the extracted BET surface areas for samples V2C (7.6 m2 g−1) and V2C@Se (5.3 m2 g−1).

The text in Results and discussion describing Fig. 1(b) explicitly states: "In the XRD pattern of V2C@Se, the (002) peak of the crystal plane disappears, and the main peak of it characterizes the selenium element"—i.e., the V2C (002) peak disappears and selenium peaks dominate. This matches the extracted note for sample V2C@Se (even though the provenance page/figure reference is slightly off; the supporting statement is on page 2 and Fig. 1(b) is shown on page 3).

The paper explicitly states in the Results and discussion section describing Fig. 1(f–i) HRTEM images: “The layer spacing of V2C and V2C@Se is about 1.08 nm and 0.97 nm, respectively.” This directly supports the extracted interlayer spacings for samples V2C and V2C@Se. Provenance is slightly off (the statement appears on the text of page 2; the figure itself is on page 3), but the values are clearly supported by the full text.

The paper explicitly reports at 1 A g−1: (i) initial discharge capacities of V2C and V2C@Se as 208.8 and 402.5 mAh g−1 (Results & discussion text referencing Fig. 2(a,b)); and (ii) after 1000 cycles at 1 A g−1, discharge specific capacities of V2C and V2C@Se as 31.5 and 119.8 mAh g−1 (text describing Fig. 2(f), also echoed in the abstract and introduction). These match the extracted values exactly. Provenance page numbering is slightly off (values appear in the text on pp. 1–3 and Fig. 2 on p. 4), but the content is supported.

The source text explicitly reports the CV redox peak positions for both V2C and V2C@Se in the Results and discussion section describing Fig. 2(g): V2C has two (reduction/oxidation) peak pairs A1/A2 at ~1.60/1.70 V and B1/B2 at ~1.75/2.20 V; V2C@Se has peak pairs at ~1.55/1.90 V and ~1.75/2.23 V. This matches the extracted notes. Provenance page label is off (the text appears on the page labeled 140 in the provided excerpt), but the values are clearly supported.

The paper explicitly reports performance data “even after 1000 cycles” and shows cycling performance “over 1000 cycles” (Fig. 2f). The abstract states 119.8 mAh g−1 remained after 1000 cycles, and the Results section repeats: “after 1000 cycles, the discharge specific capacity of V2C@Se is still 119.8 mAh g−1…”. Thus the cycle life of the tested cathode is 1000 cycles, matching the extracted value.
